notes: Object insert through has_species, the inverse of in_genus. "A species belongs to the family of its genus" and "Pongo is in Hominidae" are one class axiom over in_family. Every entity is distinct: the record calls the species newly described, none of the three named ones. The 'only' question (q3) is determinate no: adding the closed list of three to the KB is inconsistent with the new, distinct living species. The two worlds differ only on the count (fol), so they carry no axioms. (2026-10-31: q3 was indeterminate with w1 keeping the closed list as an exception world; the record now makes it determinate, FINDINGS A1.) "Hominidae are apes" is written through a class of the family individual (ApeFamily), not as "in_family value hominidae ⊑ Ape": with that form reason.py's q0 probe (the same class expression) was not reported as entailed though HermiT entails it (owlready2 equivalent-class probe issue).

background.pongo_family: in_genus value pongo ⊑ in_family value hominidae

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): counts the members of a group

queries.ask: LivingSpecies and in_genus value pongo ⊑ {bornean, sumatran, tapanuli}

fol.notes: Species are an uninterpreted sort, one constant per orangutan species the model knows (the three named in w2's chain and q3); being in the genus Pongo and living are beliefs (uninterpreted predicates). w1 stores the count as a figure (number_of_members, ATTRIBUTES.md), which the insert does not recompute; w2 stores the counting rule over the stored list (each named member counted once: an entry counts only if it differs from the earlier ones, so the distinctness presupposition enters the count). Counting needs a closed world: the known members are distinct and every member the model knows is one of the named constants (presuppositions; named_only is what the counting rule rests on, though Z3 does not need it to fix the value). The new member's distinctness from the named ones is part of the edit ('newly described/discovered').

three_orangutans.says: The Bornean, Sumatran and Tapanuli orangutans are living species of the genus Pongo. (stored, as a list)

distinct_known.says: The three named orangutans are three different species. (closed world)

named_only.says: Every living orangutan species the model knows of is one of the named species. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(s, Implies(And(in_pongo(s), living(s)), Or(s == bornean, s == sumatran, s == tapanuli, s == sinarensis)))

edit: And(sinarensis != bornean, sinarensis != sumatran, sinarensis != tapanuli)

stores: number_of_members(orangutans) == count(And(in_pongo(bornean), living(bornean)), And(And(in_pongo(sumatran), living(sumatran)), bornean != sumatran), And(And(in_pongo(tapanuli), living(tapanuli)), bornean != tapanuli, sumatran != tapanuli), And(And(in_pongo(sinarensis), living(sinarensis)), bornean != sinarensis, sumatran != sinarensis, tapanuli != sinarensis))
